title: Session-scope error snapshot proposals
content:
Purpose:
This working doc proposes a ‘session-scope error snapshot’ view for the Console’s diagnostics workbench. Goal is to give engineers a single, shareable canvas that captures a failing user session (one or more requests) across layers: API gateway logs, runtime traces, model outputs, and user-visible errors.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Current investigator flows require hopping between the request list, traces, and raw logs. Hard to get a coherent timeline across token-level model failures (e.g., hallucination detection), 5xxs, and upstream timeouts.
- Support/customer teams need a quick summary to share with customers that shows what failed and why without dumping raw logs.
- We want a canonical artifact for postmortems and regressions (saved snapshot tied to a rollout).

Primary personas:
- Platform SRE: needs latency heatmap and fallback chain to identify infra regressions.
- Model ops / Applied ML: needs token-level model output, logits/entropy spikes, and model variant versions.
- Integrations engineer / customer success: wants simple TL;DR, payloads, and whether privacy redaction removed any fields.

High-level user journey:
1) User filters Requests list (time range, route, customer id) -> selects one or multiple requests -> clicks ‘Create session snapshot’ or opens existing snapshot attached to an incident.
2) Session snapshot loads a 3-column canvas: (A) Timeline + request metadata, (B) Expanded request cards with model/infra diagnostics, (C) Context panel with traces, logs, and saved artifacts.
3) User annotates, adds tags, and exports snapshot (PDF/Share link) or pins it to a rollout for quality regression tracking.

Wireframe notes (low-fi):
- Canvas header: session id, time window, route, customer, snapshot status (draft / saved / linked-to-incident). Buttons: Export, Pin to rollout, Add note, Re-run diff.
- Left column (Timeline): compact vertical timeline with time markers. Each request point expands inline to show HTTP status, latency, tokens generated, model variant, and error badges (timeout/5xx/model-error). Hover shows small flame icon if new error type compared to baseline.
- Middle column (Request cards): stacked cards per request. Card collapsed state: summary row (status, latency, token count, top error). Expanded state: request/response payload (with redact toggle), token timeline visualization (per-token perplexity or surprisal plotted as small sparkline), model metadata (quantization, kernel used), last stable model version for comparison.
- Right column (Context + Tools): trace waterfall (service spans), raw logs with quick-search, cached prefix entries, relevant reroute/fallback history, and a small panel for 'Suggested next steps' generated by rules (e.g., suggest increasing timeout, check model route fallback).
- Bottom bar: quick metrics strip (median latency, error rate for session, token cost estimate), links to related alerts and incident page.

Interactions / micro-flows:
- Save snapshot: capture attached artifacts (trace id, logs link, model metadata, recent deployments). Snapshot becomes immutable after ‘save’ (editable copies allowed).
- Compare snapshots: diff two session snapshots side-by-side; highlight changed model versions, backend latencies, and changes in perplexity spikes.
- Auto-annotate: when snapshot created from alerts, auto-tag suspected cause (e.g., infra-timeout, model-oom, tokenization mismatch) with confidence score. Users can accept/reject tags.

Data model assumptions (for engineering):
- Snapshot object stores: session id, request ids[], start/end timestamp, trace ids[], model_versions[], token_statistics (array of numbers), host_pods[], links to raw logs (S3), and a snapshot status.
- Snapshots are lightweight pointers to artifacts, not full data blobs (but option to include inline payloads when user opts-in).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create snapshot from single request in request-list.
- View timeline + expanded request card + trace waterfall.
- Export snapshot as PDF and copyable share link.
- Pin to rollout and render in rollout timeline.

Backlog / grooming items (rough priorities and T-shirt estimates):
- PS-01: Snapshot schema + persistence model (backend) — Priority: high — Est: M (3w)
- PS-02: Timeline component + compact request marker UI — Priority: high — Est: S (1w)
- PS-03: Token-level sparkline visualization (per-request) — Priority: med — Est: S (1w)
- PS-04: Trace waterfall embed + log quicksearch — Priority: high — Est: M (2w)
- PS-05: Export to PDF + share links + ACL checks — Priority: high — Est: M (2w)
- PS-06: Snapshot compare view (two-up) — Priority: med — Est: L (3w)
- PS-07: Auto-annotation rules and confidence heuristics — Priority: low — Est: M (3w)
- PS-08: Redaction controls and privacy audit trail — Priority: high (legal) — Est: M (3w)
- PS-09: Pin to rollout integration + rollback link — Priority: med — Est: S (1w)

UI polish / design considerations:
- Use color-limited palette for error badges: infra-timeout (amber), 5xx (red), model-error (purple), degraded-quality (orange). Keep icons small, rely on text for accessibility.
- Token sparklines should be high-contrast with optional smoothing. Tooltips display absolute perplexity/value and token index.
- Collapsed cards should display a privacy-safe blurb; default redact PII.
- Mobile: support read-only views and export; editing reserved for desktop.

Telemetry / metrics to track after launch:
- Snapshot creation rate per team and per route.
- Avg time-to-annotate/close a snapshot.
- % snapshots pinned to rollouts.
- Export/share link usage and permission-denied events.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
1) Inline payloads vs pointers: full inclusion increases snapshot portability but pulls sensitive data into the Console; prefer pointers with opt-in inline. 2) How much of token-level model state to surface (logits vs entropy)? Logits are useful but large and sensitive. Start with derived metrics (entropy, perplexity) and sample logits on-demand. 3) Snapshot lifecycle: TTL? retention tied to customer retention periods and compliance — need legal input.

Dependencies / integrations:
- Trace + logs (SRE infra team) for easy pointer resolution.
- Rollout service (product-console) for pinning.
- Authz/ACL (security) for share links.
- Model registry (applied-ml) for baseline model comparisons.

Prototype notes (for design pairing):
- Quick prototype in Figma: build three-column layout with collapsible cards. Minimal interactions: expand/collapse, redact toggle, export modal. Link: (Figma file internal) — see linked_artifacts.
- Dev experiment: implement timeline as react-virtualized list to support sessions with dozens of requests. Use small sparklines rendered in canvas for perf.

Next steps / immediate actions (owner = Priya):
- Spin up async design sync with Ethan and Maya to lock primary interactions (by 2026-03-05).
- Create JIRA epic PS-SNAPSHOT and ticketize backlog items (by 2026-03-10).
- Sprint proposal: target MVP for internal dogfood in Sprint 2026-04.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working draft — feedback desirable on the compare UX and the minimal dataset we should ship in MVP.
- Slack thread for discussion: #console-error-explorer (see kickoff: slack thread ID in linked_artifacts).

Choppy / working fragments below (left intentionally):
- consider ‘heatmap overlay’ that flags clusters of token anomalies across session instead of per-request only
- what about multi-model sessions (customer A routes to model X then fallback to Y)? should snapshot show both on same timeline or split lanes? leaning single timeline with model-variant badges.
- legal: retention + redaction must be opt-out default; ask compliance for baseline policy.

Ownership history / change log:
- 2025-11-18: initial outline (Priya)
- 2026-01-04: added compare-snapshots concept (Ethan)
- 2026-02-25: updated backlog estimates and acceptance criteria (Maya)

End of doc.
